title: What Is an ITIN Number and How Does It Work?
seo_title: What Is an ITIN Number? | ITIN Pro UK
meta_description: An ITIN is a 9-digit IRS tax number for people who can't get an SSN. Learn who needs one, how Form W-7 works and how UK applicants keep their passport.

hook: A US bank, broker or tax adviser has just asked for your "ITIN" and you have never heard the word before. Don't worry, it's simpler than it sounds.
quick_answer: An ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number) is a 9-digit number issued by the IRS, always starting with 9, for people who need a US tax ID but cannot get a Social Security Number. It is used only for US tax purposes. You apply on Form W-7, usually alongside a US tax return.

scenario.name: Priya
scenario.story: Priya, a pharmacist in Reading, inherited a small share of her late uncle's US investment account. The US custodian wrote asking for her "US TIN" before releasing the funds, and mentioned that otherwise 30% could be withheld. She has never lived in America and cannot get a Social Security Number. After a short call, she learned the number she needed was an ITIN, and that a Certifying Acceptance Agent could check her passport in person, so it never had to leave her hands. (Scenario is illustrative.)

sections.h2: An ITIN in plain English
sections.body_md:
Think of an ITIN as a tax reference number from the IRS, a little like a UTR from HMRC.

It exists so the IRS can track tax returns and payments for people who are not eligible for a Social Security Number (SSN). It is nine digits long and always begins with 9.

What an ITIN is **not** matters just as much:

- It is not permission to work in the US.
- It does not change your immigration status.
- It is not an ID card for anything other than tax.

sections.h2: What you need to apply
sections.body_md:
The application form is **Form W-7**. On it you tick one reason box, such as box b for a nonresident filing a US return.

Most first-time applicants attach a US federal tax return, often **Form 1040-NR**. Some people qualify for an exception instead, for example when a US payer or bank needs the number for withholding purposes.

You also need proof of identity and foreign status:

- A valid passport is the only document that works on its own.
- Otherwise you need two documents from the IRS list of 13.
- They must be originals or copies certified by the **issuing agency**. Copies certified by a solicitor or notary are not accepted.

sections.h2: How the process works, step by step
sections.body_md:
1. **Check you need one.** Not everyone with a US connection does.
2. **Prepare Form W-7** and your return or exception paperwork.
3. **Have your ID verified.** A Certifying Acceptance Agent (CAA) checks your original passport and signs a certificate, Form W-7 (COA). You keep your passport.
4. **The CAA sends the package to the IRS.**
5. **Wait for the IRS letter.** Your number arrives on notice CP565.

The IRS says to allow about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season (15 January to 30 April) or when applying from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September applications often take about 7 weeks, and from October it is often 4 to 6 weeks. No one can promise a time.

sections.h2: Common mistakes we see
sections.body_md:
- **Sending a solicitor-certified copy** of a passport. The IRS will reject it.
- **Applying without a reason.** You need a return to file or a valid exception.
- **Posting your original passport to the US** when a CAA could check it in the UK.
- **Letting an ITIN lapse.** It expires if not used on a US federal return for three tax years in a row.

faqs.q: What is an ITIN number used for?
faqs.a: An ITIN is used to file US federal tax returns, claim treaty benefits and let US payers report income for people who cannot get an SSN. Typical UK users include property sellers, investors, beneficiaries of US estates and people claiming refunds of US tax withheld from winnings or pensions.

faqs.q: Is an ITIN the same as a Social Security Number?
faqs.a: An ITIN is not the same as a Social Security Number. An SSN is for people allowed to work in the US and links to social security benefits. An ITIN is only a tax processing number for people who are not eligible for an SSN, and it gives no right to work or benefits.

faqs.q: Can I get an ITIN if I live in the UK?
faqs.a: An ITIN can be issued to UK residents who have a US tax reason, such as filing a return or meeting an IRS exception. You do not need to visit the US. A Certifying Acceptance Agent in the UK can verify your passport so you do not post it to the IRS.

faqs.q: How long does an ITIN take?
faqs.a: An ITIN usually takes about 7 weeks after the IRS receives a complete application, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season (15 January to 30 April) or from abroad, according to the IRS. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, while applications from October often come back in 4 to 6 weeks. Errors add further delay.

faqs.q: Does an ITIN ever expire?
faqs.a: An ITIN expires if it is not used on a US federal tax return for three consecutive tax years. It lapses on 31 December of the third year. You renew with Form W-7 and a tax return, but only when you actually need to file.

faqs.q: Do I need an ITIN to fill in a W-8BEN?
faqs.a: An ITIN is not always needed for Form W-8BEN. Many UK residents can enter a UK tax number, such as a National Insurance number or UTR, to claim treaty rates. You usually need an ITIN when you must file a US return or a payer insists on one.

takeaway: An ITIN is a US tax number only, not a work permit or visa.
You normally apply with Form W-7 plus a US tax return or a valid exception.
A CAA lets you keep your passport instead of posting it to the IRS.

sections.h2: What a Certifying Acceptance Agent actually does
sections.body_md:
A CAA is a person or firm authorised by the IRS to help with ITIN applications and to **authenticate identity documents**.

That last part is the key. Without a CAA, you usually have to post your original passport, or a copy certified by the passport office, to the IRS.

With a CAA, the agent examines your original, completes **Form W-7 (COA)** to certify it, and sends that certificate with your application. Your passport goes home with you.

A CAA does not issue ITINs. The IRS decides every application.

title: Do I Need an ITIN to Open a US LLC as a Non-Resident?
seo_title: Do I Need an ITIN for a US LLC? | ITIN Pro UK
meta_description: A non-resident can form a US LLC and get an EIN without an ITIN. Learn when an LLC owner does need an ITIN and how UK founders set up correctly.
secondary_keywords: do I need an ITIN to open an LLC
single member LLC foreign owner Form 5472
hook: You have set up a Delaware or Wyoming LLC, and now a form asks for an SSN or ITIN. Most UK founders assume they are stuck. Usually, they are not.
quick_answer: An ITIN is not needed to form a US LLC or obtain its EIN. A foreign owner can apply for an EIN on Form SS-4 without one. An ITIN becomes necessary when the owner must file a personal US return, such as Form 1040-NR, or a bank, payer or partnership requires it.

scenario.name: Callum
scenario.story: Callum, a software developer in Glasgow, set up a single-member Wyoming LLC to invoice American clients. The online formation was easy, but the EIN page kept asking for his SSN or ITIN, and a forum post told him to apply for an ITIN first. He paused everything. In fact, as a foreign owner he could apply for the EIN on Form SS-4 without an ITIN. He got the EIN, opened his business account, and learned that his LLC would need to file Form 5472 with a pro-forma 1120 each year. (Scenario is illustrative.)

sections.h2: EIN versus ITIN: two different numbers
sections.body_md:
An **EIN** (Employer Identification Number) identifies a business. An **ITIN** identifies an individual for tax.

Your LLC needs an EIN to open a US bank account, work with payment platforms and file its own returns. You apply for it on **Form SS-4**.

A foreign owner with no SSN or ITIN can still get an EIN. The online system often expects a US number, which is why many non-residents apply by fax or post instead.

sections.h2: When an LLC owner does need an ITIN
sections.body_md:
An ITIN comes into play when **you personally** have a US filing requirement or someone insists on a personal US tax number. Common triggers:

- Your LLC is taxed as a partnership (two or more owners). A foreign investor in it needs an ITIN. The LLC generally withholds tax on your share of US business income and reports it on **Form 8805**; that tax is credited on your **Form 1040-NR**, which needs an ITIN, so you can reclaim any excess.
- You must file **Form 1040-NR** for income effectively connected with a US trade or business.
- You want to claim a refund of US tax withheld.
- A US bank, payer or partnership asks for an individual TIN.

If none of these apply, you may not need one at all.

sections.h2: What a single-member foreign-owned LLC files
sections.body_md:
A single-member LLC owned by a non-resident is generally treated as a "disregarded entity". Even so, it has a yearly reporting duty.

- **Form 5472**, reporting transactions between the LLC and its foreign owner.
- A **pro-forma Form 1120** as a cover sheet.

This uses the LLC's **EIN**, not an ITIN. Whether you also need a personal return depends on how and where your income is earned, so take advice on your own facts.

sections.h2: Common mistakes UK founders make
sections.body_md:
- **Applying for an ITIN just to get an EIN.** It is usually unnecessary and adds weeks.
- **Ignoring Form 5472.** Single-member foreign-owned LLCs must file it even with little activity.
- **Mixing up the numbers** on bank or payment forms. The business uses its EIN; you use an ITIN only where a personal TIN is truly required.
- **Assuming no US tax return is needed** when you invest in an LLC taxed as a partnership. You need an ITIN and a 1040-NR to reclaim Form 8805 withholding.

faqs.q: Can a non-resident get an EIN without an ITIN?
faqs.a: A non-resident can get an EIN without an ITIN. On Form SS-4 a foreign individual with no SSN or ITIN can still apply. Because the online system usually expects a US number, many foreign owners apply by fax or post instead.

faqs.q: Do I need an ITIN to open a US business bank account for my LLC?
faqs.a: An ITIN is usually not required to open a business account for an LLC, which uses its EIN. However, some banks and fintech providers ask the owner for a personal US tax number as part of their own checks. If yours insists, an ITIN may become necessary.

faqs.q: Does a single-member LLC owned by a UK resident file a US tax return?
faqs.a: A single-member LLC owned by a UK resident generally files Form 5472 with a pro-forma Form 1120 each year, using its EIN. Whether the owner must also file a personal Form 1040-NR depends on the type and source of the income.

faqs.q: When does an LLC owner need an ITIN?
faqs.a: An LLC owner needs an ITIN when they personally must file a US return, such as Form 1040-NR for effectively connected income or a K-1 from a multi-member LLC, want to claim a US refund, or when a bank, payer or partnership requires a personal US TIN.

faqs.q: Is an EIN the same as an ITIN?
faqs.a: An EIN is not the same as an ITIN. An EIN is issued to a business on Form SS-4. An ITIN is issued to an individual on Form W-7. Many UK founders need only the EIN, at least at the start.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to get an EIN from the UK?
faqs.a: An EIN costs nothing from the IRS directly. If you want help, ITIN Pro UK charges £375 all-inclusive, with no VAT, to prepare and file the EIN application. An ITIN, if you later need one, is a separate £450 service.

faqs.q: Does a foreign investor in a US LLC taxed as a partnership need an ITIN?
faqs.a: Yes, a foreign investor in a US LLC taxed as a partnership needs an ITIN. The LLC withholds tax on your share of effectively connected income and reports it on Form 8805. That tax is credited on your Form 1040-NR, which needs an ITIN, so you can reclaim any excess. The LLC's own EIN still doesn't depend on your ITIN.

takeaway: Your LLC needs an EIN; you personally may not need an ITIN.
Single-member foreign-owned LLCs file Form 5472 with a pro-forma 1120.
Get an ITIN when you must file a personal return or a payer insists.

title: ITIN for a Partnership Interest: A Guide for UK K-1 Investors
seo_title: ITIN for Partnership K-1 Investors | ITIN Pro UK
meta_description: Got a US partnership K-1 as a UK investor? Learn when you need an ITIN, how Exception 1(a) works and how to reclaim withholding on Form 1040-NR.
secondary_keywords: K-1 investor ITIN help near me
hook: A US fund or property partnership has sent you a K-1 and a request for your "US taxpayer ID". You have no idea what either really means.
quick_answer: An ITIN for a partnership interest lets a foreign partner be identified on Schedule K-1 and withholding forms, and file Form 1040-NR to claim credit for tax withheld. Under Exception 1(a), you can apply before filing a return, using evidence of the partnership interest.

scenario.name: Elena
scenario.story: Elena, a research scientist in Cambridge, invested $50,000 (about £39,000) in a US real estate limited partnership through a former colleague. At year end she received a Schedule K-1 and a Form 8805 showing tax the partnership had withheld on her share of US business income. The partnership's accountant also asked for her ITIN. Without one, she could not file a 1040-NR to claim credit for the withholding. She applied under Exception 1(a) using her partnership documents, then filed once her ITIN arrived. (Scenario is illustrative.)

sections.h2: Why partnerships ask foreign partners for an ITIN
sections.body_md:
A US partnership reports each partner's share of income on **Schedule K-1**. To do that properly, it needs a tax number for every partner.

When a partnership earns income connected with a US business, it generally has to withhold tax on a foreign partner's share. It reports that on **Form 8805** (or Form 1042-S for some income types).

To get credit for that withholding, the foreign partner files **Form 1040-NR**, and that return needs an ITIN. If more was withheld than you owe, the excess is refunded.

The same applies to a **US LLC taxed as a partnership**: a foreign investor in it needs an ITIN to claim the Form 8805 withholding back.

sections.h2: What you need: Exception 1(a)
sections.body_md:
Normally a first-time ITIN application goes with a tax return. **Exception 1(a)** lets a foreign partner apply earlier, based on the partnership interest itself.

Typical paperwork includes:

- **Form W-7**, with Exception 1(a) noted as your reason for applying.
- **A copy of the partnership agreement** or similar evidence of your interest, with your name and the partnership's EIN.
- **Your passport,** verified by a Certifying Acceptance Agent so you keep the original.

Applying early means your number can be ready before the filing deadline.

sections.h2: How it works, step by step
sections.body_md:
1. **Gather your K-1, Form 8805 and partnership agreement.**
2. **Decide your route:** Exception 1(a) now, or W-7 with your first 1040-NR.
3. **Have your passport verified** by a CAA.
4. **Send the application** and wait: typically 7 to 13 weeks, depending on the season.
5. **Give the ITIN to the partnership** and file your 1040-NR to claim credit for tax withheld.

Selling your stake later? A buyer of a partnership interest generally withholds **10%** under section 1446(f), so plan ahead.

sections.h2: Common mistakes K-1 investors make
sections.body_md:
- **Ignoring the K-1** because "it's only a small amount". Withholding you never claim is simply lost.
- **Sending a solicitor-certified passport copy.** Only originals or issuing-agency certified copies are accepted.
- **Confusing your ITIN with the partnership's EIN.** The partnership has its own number; you need yours.
- **Waiting until a sale** to sort out your ITIN, when the 10% withholding is already in play.

faqs.q: Do I need an ITIN if I receive a K-1 as a non-resident?
faqs.a: An ITIN is needed if you receive a K-1 as a foreign partner, including as an investor in a US LLC taxed as a partnership. sections.h2: What FIRPTA is, in plain English
sections.body_md:
FIRPTA is a US law that makes sure foreign sellers of US property pay their tax.

When a foreign person sells, the buyer generally withholds **15% of the gross sale price**, not the profit, and sends it to the IRS on **Forms 8288 and 8288-A**. Lower rates of 10% or 0% can apply when the buyer will live in the home and the price is up to $1 million or $300,000.

That withholding is a prepayment, not your final bill. If your real tax is lower, you claim the difference back.

sections.h2: What you need to claim it back
sections.body_md:
- **An ITIN** for each seller, applied for on **Form W-7**.
- **Form 1040-NR**, reporting the sale and your actual gain.
- **Copy B of Form 8288-A**, showing the tax withheld.
- **The sale contract and closing statement.**
- **Purchase records and improvement costs,** which raise your cost base and reduce your gain.

If you own jointly, each owner normally needs their own ITIN and return. Some US states also withhold on sales, so check your closing statement for state amounts too.

sections.h2: How the refund process works
sections.body_md:
1. **Apply for your ITIN.** Under Exception 4 you can apply with the sale paperwork rather than a return.
2. **Have your passport verified** by a CAA so it stays with you.
3. **Collect Copy B of Form 8288-A** once the IRS processes the buyer's filing.
4. **File Form 1040-NR** after the tax year ends, with Copy B attached.
5. **Wait for the IRS** to process the return and issue any refund.

Haven't closed yet? A **Form 8288-B** withholding certificate may reduce withholding at closing, and it also needs an ITIN. Form W-7 goes in together with Form 8288-B only when you are applying for a withholding certificate, and certain conditions must be met. sections.h2: Common mistakes foreign sellers make

- **Losing Copy B of Form 8288-A.** It is your proof of tax paid.
- **Forgetting improvement costs,** which can reduce your gain significantly.
- **Only one spouse applying** when the property was jointly owned.

faqs.q: When can I file for my FIRPTA refund?
faqs.a: A FIRPTA refund is normally claimed after the end of the US tax year in which you sold, by filing Form 1040-NR. For a sale in 2026, that means filing in 2027. Having your ITIN ready by then avoids extra delay.

sections.h2: What you need before you apply

The IRS needs to know exactly who is selling. That means each foreign seller needs a US taxpayer number, which for most UK individuals is an **ITIN**.

You apply for the ITIN on **Form W-7** under Exception 4 (FIRPTA). Form W-7 is filed together with Form 8288-B only when you are applying for a withholding certificate (reduced or no withholding), and certain conditions must be met. - A copy of the signed sale contract
- Form 8288-B (or Forms 8288 and 8288-A after closing)
- Your passport, seen by a Certifying Acceptance Agent, or an original or issuing-agency certified copy

5. **After the tax year**, you file **Form 1040-NR** with Copy B of Form 8288-A to claim credit for what was withheld, and a refund of any excess.

sections.h2: What a 1040-NR is, in plain English
sections.body_md:
Form 1040-NR is the US federal tax return for **nonresident aliens**. That covers most people who live in the UK but have some US income or US tax taken from them.

Every return needs a taxpayer number. If you can't get an SSN, that number is an **ITIN**: a 9-digit number starting with 9, used only for tax.

An ITIN is not a work permit, a visa or a form of US ID.

sections.h2: Who usually ends up filing
sections.body_md:
People we commonly help include those who:

- had **tax withheld and want it back**, such as UK residents with US casino winnings
- **sold US property** and had FIRPTA tax withheld
- receive a **K-1** from a US partnership with business income
- had **backup withholding** after a W-8BEN expired

Not everyone with US income must file. If the right treaty rate was applied at source, there may be nothing to do. Check before you assume.

sections.h2: What you need and how it works
sections.body_md:
For a first-time ITIN, the application and the return travel together:

1. **Prepare Form 1040-NR**, leaving the ID number space for the IRS to complete.
2. **Complete Form W-7**, usually ticking box b (nonresident filing a US return).
3. **Verify identity** with your passport. A CAA checks it and returns it to you.
4. **Post the package** to the IRS ITIN unit.
5. **Wait for Notice CP565**, your ITIN assignment letter. The IRS says about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 weeks in peak season or from abroad. In our experience, April to July can take 12 to 13 weeks, September about 7, and from October often 4 to 6.

A return can't be e-filed in the calendar year your ITIN is issued, so the first one goes on paper.

sections.h2: Common mistakes to avoid
sections.body_md:
- **Sending the W-7 on its own.** Without a return or a valid exception, it will normally be rejected.
- **Using notarised copies** of your passport. Only originals or issuing-agency certified copies count.
- **Ignoring Form 1042-S.** It shows the US income and tax withheld, and the return relies on it.
- **Filing a 1040 instead of a 1040-NR** when you are a nonresident.

faqs.q: Can I file a 1040-NR without an ITIN or SSN?
faqs.a: No, a Form 1040-NR needs a US taxpayer number, and nonresidents who can't get an SSN use an ITIN. If you don't have one yet, you apply on Form W-7 and attach your first 1040-NR, so the IRS assigns the ITIN and processes the return.

faqs.q: Do I need to file a 1040-NR if tax was already withheld?
faqs.a: A 1040-NR is often optional when the correct amount was withheld, but it is the only way to get back tax that was over-withheld. If you want a refund, for example of casino or FIRPTA withholding, you need to file, and that means getting an ITIN.

faqs.q: Can I e-file my first 1040-NR with a new ITIN?
faqs.a: No, a return can't be e-filed in the calendar year your ITIN is received. For a first-time application, you post the paper 1040-NR together with Form W-7 anyway, so plan for postal timescales rather than an online submission. Later years can usually be e-filed once the ITIN is active.

faqs.q: Which box do I tick on Form W-7 for a 1040-NR?
faqs.a: Most nonresidents filing a 1040-NR tick box b on Form W-7, which means a nonresident alien filing a US federal tax return. If you're also claiming a treaty benefit or using an exception, a different box may apply, so check before you send.

faqs.q: What is Form 1042-S and why does it matter for my 1040-NR?
faqs.a: Form 1042-S reports US-source income paid to a foreign person and any tax withheld. You use it to complete your 1040-NR and claim credit for that withholding. If you got a 1099 instead, your payer may treat you as a US person, which needs fixing.

faqs.q: How long does a refund take after filing a 1040-NR with Form W-7?
faqs.a: The IRS says the ITIN takes about 7 weeks, or 9 to 11 from abroad; in our experience it's typically 7 to 13 weeks depending on the season, before the return is processed. The refund follows after that, so expect the whole process to take a few months rather than weeks.

The IRS uses a few notice numbers for ITIN problems. The two you're most likely to see are:

- **CP567**: your application has been rejected. It is closed.

In our experience, most rejections come down to a handful of avoidable issues:

- **Wrong kind of copy.** Notarised or solicitor-certified copies are not accepted. Only originals or copies certified by the issuing agency are.

- **Reason box doesn't fit.** For example, ticking box a without the treaty exception details, or box h without writing in the exception.
- **Dependant paperwork.** Dependants may need extra proof, such as a US entry stamp or evidence of US residency.
- **Not enough documents.** A passport works alone. Otherwise you need two acceptable documents.
